atoms.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Maxie wants to compare a UK town to other towns around the world.

instruction.text: Answer Maxie’s question by listening to the options and selecting the correct answer.

feedback.end: It’s a great idea to talk with local people to learn more about the place they live in. Just make sure to be friendly and polite!

atoms.a: “How can we learn more about a town when doing fieldwork?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>How can we learn more about a town when doing fieldwork?</prosody></voice>

b.sound: We can talk with the animals and ask them if they like this area.
We can talk with the local people of an area to ask them about their lives here.

atoms.text: Maxie is bringing this photo of Ayr with him to compare with other towns. Let’s visit a Kenyan town in Africa first!

atoms.a: “What do you not see in this town compared to Ayr?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>What do you not see in this town compared to Ayr?</prosody></voice>

atoms.a: “Do the houses look the same as in Ayr or different?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>Do the houses look the same as in Ayr or different?</prosody></voice>

feedback.end: Many towns and villages around the world don’t have roads like in the UK. People get around just by walking, riding bikes or even driving boats!

atoms.text: Now let’s bring this photo to a Puerto Rican town in the Caribbean!

atoms.a: “What is different about the houses in this town?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>What is different about the houses in this town?</prosody></voice>

atoms.a: “Are the houses close together or far apart?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>Are the houses close together or far apart?</prosody></voice>

feedback.end: In some towns around the world, houses are closely packed together and built on different levels. The streets are also often much narrower.

atoms.text: Now let’s bring this photo to a Thai village in Asia!

atoms.a: “What do you see a lot more of here than in Ayr?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>What do you see a lot more of here than in Ayr?</prosody></voice>

atoms.a: “Are the streets narrower or wider here?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>Are the streets narrower or wider here?</prosody></voice>

feedback.end: Culture and traditions play a role in how a town looks. This is partly why houses look so different around the world!

atoms.text: Finally, let’s bring this photo to a Peruvian town in South America!

atoms.a: “Does this town look flatter or hillier than Ayr?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>Does this town look flatter or hillier than Ayr?</prosody></voice>

atoms.a: “What do you see here that isn’t in Ayr?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'><prosody pitch = '+2st'>What do you see here that isn’t in Ayr?</prosody></voice>

feedback.end: The way a town looks also depends a lot on the natural landscape there. A town in the mountains will look very different from a town built on flat land!
